defaultDescription: Sigvault is a self-hosted post-quantum token issuer and verifier. ML-DSA-87 (FIPS 204) and Falcon signatures, encrypted claims, structural replay protection, and a server with zero npm dependencies.

routes.title: Sigvault — post-quantum tokens you can run yourself
routes.description: Sigvault is a self-hosted post-quantum token issuer and verifier. ML-DSA-87 (FIPS 204) and Falcon signatures, encrypted claims, structural replay protection, and a server with zero npm dependencies.

routes.title: Quickstart — issue and verify a post-quantum token in 60 seconds
routes.description: Install @sigvault/sdk, sigvault (Python), or qv-core (Rust), generate a key triplet, and verify your first ML-DSA-87 or Falcon-signed token.

routes.title: Live demo — sign a post-quantum token in your browser
routes.description: Generate ML-DSA-87 keys, issue an encrypted token, verify it, then tamper with one byte and watch verification fail. Runs entirely in your browser.

routes.title: Post-quantum migration timeline — NIST, CNSA 2.0, EU, and what to do now
routes.description: The dates that matter: NIST IR 8547 deprecates RSA and ECDSA in 2030 and disallows them in 2035. CNSA 2.0, EU and UK roadmaps. How token signing fits in.

routes.title: AI-era threat model — why structure beats detection
routes.description: AI makes replay, credential stuffing, dependency poisoning and token forgery cheap and parallel. Eight attacks and the structural control in Sigvault that closes each one, with links to the code.

routes.title: How Sigvault works — key triplet, suites, mutation chain
routes.description: The five ideas behind Sigvault: the key triplet, post-quantum signature suites, AEAD-sealed claims, the mutation chain, and stateless verification.

routes.title: Architecture — one process, one wire format, any backend
routes.description: How the Sigvault server, ChainStore backends, SDKs, FFI binaries and WASM bundle fit together and share a single conformance suite.

routes.title: Storybook — 22 chapters on the reasoning behind Sigvault
routes.description: Why Sigvault exists, how each layer works, and what was deliberately left out. Twenty-two chapters from the threat model to operations.

routes.title: About Sigvault — who builds it and how to reach us
routes.description: Sigvault is built by independent contributors. Licences, contact, security disclosure, and the principles behind the project.

routes.title: Privacy policy — Sigvault
routes.description: What this site collects, what it does not, and how the in-browser demo keeps your keys on your device.

routes.title: Terms of use — Sigvault
routes.description: Terms for using this website and the open-source Sigvault software it documents.
